les: Geraas, en hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
kaps_punt: Geraasbesoedeling. Klanke wat hard, onaangenaam of skadelik vir ons ore is of oor 'n lang periode strek, word beskryf as geraasbesoedeling; geraasbesoedeling kan permanente skade aan die gehoor veroorsaak (gehoorapparate kan help om mense wat gehoorgestremd is te laat hoor).

items.bewering: Klank wat so pla, het 'n eie naam: geraasbesoedeling.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n klank geraas word
items.bron: US EPA, 'Clean Air Act Title IV - Noise Pollution' (epa.gov/clean-air-act-overview/clean-air-act-title-iv-noise-pollution): the traditional definition of noise is 'unwanted or disturbing sound', which becomes unwanted when it interferes with sleep, conversation or quality of life. The block's framing ('klank wat so pla') carries that core.

items.bewering: Die klank kan hard wees, soos 'n boor wat in die straat werk.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n klank geraas word
items.bron: Jackhammer/pneumatic drill figures of about 97-102 dBA at the operator or at 2 m (WSCC NT 'How loud is it' chart; e3diagnostics jobsite list); well above the 85 dBA level NIDCD names for risk (nidcd.nih.gov/health/noise-induced-hearing-loss).

items.bewering: Dit kan naar wees om na te luister, soos 'n hek wat kras.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n klank geraas word
items.bron: US EPA noise definition ('unwanted or disturbing sound'); an unpleasant sound qualifies by being disturbing, independent of loudness. Matches the CAPS criterion 'onaangenaam'.

items.bewering: Vier dinge kan 'n gewone klank in geraas verander. ... Enige een van die vier is al genoeg, en hulle hoef nie saam voor te kom nie.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n klank geraas word
items.bron: Inside this block the four criteria sit under the opening frame 'Klank wat so pla', so each is read as a way a sound becomes unwanted - consistent with the EPA definition (unwanted or disturbing sound) and with South African law's 'noise nuisance' ('noise that disturbs or impairs ... the convenience or peace of any person', BusinessTech 2019 citing Bregmans). Note: the same four criteria WITHOUT that frame are a fault in the glossary entry - see the 'geraasbesoedeling' item.

items.bewering: 'n Klank hoef nie hard te wees om geraas te wees nie. Dink aan 'n kraan wat die hele nag lank drup. Elke drup op sy eie is sag, en tog hou dit jou wakker.
items.blok: Dit hoef nie hard te wees nie
items.bron: Leon Lack, Flinders University sleep researcher, 'Drip, drip, drip: why a leaking tap keeps you awake' (sleepreviewmag.com / news.flinders.edu.au): low-intensity regular sounds such as a dripping tap can keep people from falling asleep. EPA: sound that interferes with sleep is unwanted, i.e. noise.

items.bewering: By die huis: 'n TV wat heeldag hard speel, oorfone wat te hard opgedraai is en 'n kragopwekker wat brom.
items.blok: Waar die geraasbesoedeling vandaan kom
items.bron: TV played loudly listed as noise nuisance (BusinessTech 2019, Bregmans attorneys); headphones at maximum volume 94-110 dBA (NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet, 2020); generator noise complaints in SA, e.g. Cape Town City Health ~197 generator complaints Feb 2022-Feb 2023 (Cape Times, 2 April 2023; Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr, 24 April 2023).

items.bewering: By die skool: baie kinders wat gelyk op die speelgrond skree en stoele wat oor die vloer skraap.
items.blok: Waar die geraasbesoedeling vandaan kom
items.bron: 'Shouting and talking loudly' listed among noise-nuisance examples (BusinessTech 2019, Bregmans attorneys); scraping is an unpleasant/disturbing sound under the EPA definition.

items.bewering: In die gemeenskap: verkeer en bouwerk langs die pad, luidsprekers by 'n winkel of 'n taxi en 'n partytjie wat tot laat aanhou.
items.blok: Waar die geraasbesoedeling vandaan kom
items.bron: Vehicles, power tools/machinery and loud late-night parties listed as noise nuisance/disturbing noise (BusinessTech 2019); loud taxi sound systems called noise pollution in SA (Witbank News letter, citizen.co.za/witbank-news; Briefly.co.za TikTok report); complaints about loud music at a Pretoria shopping centre (BusinessTech, May 2026) and shop-front speakers as noise pollution in the region (Nairobi, Bulawayo). Construction noise 80-90 dB typical.

items.bewering: Nie alle geraas beskadig jou ore nie, en 'n kraan se drup doen dit ook nie.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (nidcd.nih.gov/health/noise-induced-hearing-loss): sounds at or below 70 dBA, even after long exposure, are unlikely to cause hearing loss.

items.bewering: Die skade kom van klank wat te hard is of te lank aanhou.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss: 'sounds can be harmful when they are too loud, even for a brief time, or when they are both loud and long-lasting'; sounds at or below 70 dBA 'even after long exposure, are unlikely to cause hearing loss'. NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet (2020): 'A single very loud noise or long or repeated exposure to sounds at or above 85 dBA can cause hearing loss.' Duration only matters for a sound that is already loud. As written, the second branch says a long-lasting sound damages regardless of loudness - and the lesson's own drip lasts all night. It also closes a false loop with the lesson's definition: a sound that lasts long is geraasbesoedeling, and geraasbesoedeling 'kan dit veroorsaak', so a learner can conclude that any long sound harms hearing.
items.regstelling: The damage comes from sound that is very loud, even for a short time, or from loud sound that goes on for a long time. The 'lasts long' branch must carry 'loud' (e.g. 'klank wat baie hard is, of harde klank wat lank aanhou'); a soft sound that lasts long, like the drip, does not damage the ear.

items.bewering: Klank beweeg deur 'n klein gangetjie tot by jou dun trommelvlies.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, How Do We Hear? (nidcd.nih.gov/health/how-do-we-hear): sound waves 'travel through a narrow passageway called the ear canal, which leads to the eardrum'.

items.bewering: Agter daardie velletjie sit baie klein dele wat soos haartjies lyk maar nie hare is nie.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, How Do We Hear?: hair cells are 'sensory cells' in the cochlea topped by 'microscopic hair-like projections (known as stereocilia)'. Mapping holds: they look like hairs and are not hairs. 'Agter' is loose (the middle-ear bones lie between eardrum and cochlea) but true in the sense of 'further in', and the Grade 4 omission of the middle ear does not mislead.

items.bewering: Hulle vang die vibrasie op en stuur die boodskap na jou brein toe.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, How Do We Hear?: bending of the stereocilia creates an electrical signal, which the auditory nerve carries to the brain. Acceptable compression at Grade 4 (the cells start the message; a nerve carries it).

items.bewering: Klank wat te hard is, breek daardie klein dele stukkend. ... Die skade is permanent, en geraasbesoedeling kan dit veroorsaak.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss: NIHL 'can be temporary or permanent'; some loss 'disappears 16 to 48 hours later'. International Noise Awareness Day / Center for Hearing and Communication (noiseawareness.org): ringing or difficulty hearing after loud noise is a 'temporary threshold shift' that usually resolves within hours or days, though repeated exposure can make it permanent. The unqualified 'breek ... stukkend' says every too-loud sound destroys these cells. Read with the next block, which correctly calls ringing or dull ears a sign that a sound was too loud, a learner whose ears rang after a party is told her hearing is permanently broken - which is usually not so. The permanence of dead hair cells themselves is correct and should stay.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier, not the subject: too-loud sound CAN break these small parts; once they are broken they never grow back, and that damage is permanent. (E.g. 'Klank wat te hard is, kan daardie klein dele stukkend breek.') Keep the permanence sentence about broken parts as it is.

items.bewering: 'n Sny in jou vel groei weer toe, maar hierdie dele groei nooit weer aan nie.
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: NIDCD, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss: 'human hair cells don't grow back. They are gone for good.' Mammalian cochlear hair cells are not regenerated (Baylor College of Medicine, ENT 'Regeneration'; PMC7245053; Hearing Health Foundation on bird regeneration). The absolute 'nooit' holds for humans; birds and fish can regrow theirs, but the lesson speaks of 'jou ore'.

items.bewering: 'n Sny in jou vel groei weer toe, maar hierdie dele groei nooit weer aan nie. (vergelyking vel teenoor gehoorselle)
items.blok: Wat diep in jou oor breek
items.bron: Contrast mapping checked: skin wounds heal by regrowth; human cochlear hair cells do not regenerate (NIDCD; Baylor ENT). The comparison teaches exactly the point and does not invite a false extension at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Skade aan jou ore maak meestal nie seer nie, en dit bou stadig op.
items.blok: Hoe jy weet 'n klank is te hard
items.bron: noiseawareness.org (Center for Hearing and Communication): 'Noise-induced hearing loss typically occurs gradually and without pain.' NIDCD: 'the damage from noise exposure is usually gradual'. 'Meestal' is right: ASHA notes firecrackers at ~150 dBP are 'painful to the ears'.

items.bewering: Maar een baie harde klank kan dadelik skade doen. 'n Klapper wat naby jou oor afgaan, is genoeg daarvoor.
items.blok: Hoe jy weet 'n klank is te hard
items.bron: ASHA news release, July 2022: 'Fireworks at 3 feet, as well as firecrackers, can measure 150 dBP'; impulse noise above 140 dBP 'will instantly hurt a person's hearing'; a single blast can cause 'immediate and permanent hearing loss'. NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet: 'Hearing damage can happen instantly.'

items.bewering: Soms tuit jou ore of voel hulle dof nadat 'n harde klank verby is. Dit is 'n teken dat die klank te hard vir jou was.
items.blok: Hoe jy weet 'n klank is te hard
items.bron: NIDCD, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (tinnitus 'ringing, buzzing, or roaring'; sounds becoming 'muffled'); noiseawareness.org: ringing or difficulty hearing after loud noise is a temporary threshold shift, a warning sign.

items.bewering: Soms moet jy harder praat met iemand wat 'n arm se lengte van jou af staan. Dan is die geraas op daardie oomblik te hard.
items.blok: Hoe jy weet 'n klank is te hard
items.bron: CDC/NIOSH 'raised voice test': having to raise your voice to be heard at about 3 feet (arm's length) means the noise is probably over 85 dB and hearing protection should be worn (cdc.gov/niosh, 2026-118; Cal Poly EHS Hearing Conservation); Mayo Clinic Minute uses the same arm's-length check. It is a rule of thumb; the lesson's 'te hard' matches its meaning.

items.bewering: Gaan weg van 'n harde klank af, want hoe verder jy wegstaan, hoe sagter word dit.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: Sound intensity falls with distance (inverse square law, about 6 dB less per doubling of distance in open space; auditoryneuroscience.com, Sengpiel Audio). NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet: 'The best ways to protect your hearing are to avoid exposure to loud sounds, move away from the noise, or turn down the volume.'

items.bewering: Draai dit sagter as die klank uit 'n TV of 'n foon kom.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: NIDCD, Protect Your Child's Hearing: 'Turn down the volume on the TV and on music players, and move away from the noise, when possible.'

items.bewering: By oorfone speel die klank reg teen jou oor, en jy kan nie daarvan wegstaan nie. Daar help dit dat jy self kies hoe hard hulle speel.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet (headphones at maximum volume 94-110 dBA); WHO-ITU Safe Listening Devices and Systems standard (who.int) built on volume control and limits for personal audio; Mayo Clinic Minute on checking headphone volume.

items.bewering: Sit jou hande oor jou ore as jy nie kan wegkom nie.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: NIDCD Fact Sheet 'Hearing Protectors' (NIH Pub. No. 20-DC-8122, November 2020), p. 2: 'If loud noise happens suddenly or unexpectedly, cover your ears with your hands and move away from the noise, if possible.' The lesson offers it as a fallback after moving away, not as a substitute for earplugs or earmuffs, which matches the source.

items.bewering: Mense wat met harde masjiene werk, dra oorkappe of oorproppe.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: South Africa, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss Regulations 2003 (GN R307, OHS Act 85 of 1993; lawlibrary.org.za): noise-rating limit 85 dBA, approved hearing protective equipment defined as ear-muffs or ear-plugs. NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet recommends them for industrial and loud workplaces.

items.bewering: Kinders dra dit ook by harde musiek, en 'n grootmens help hulle daarmee.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: NIDCD Hearing Protectors fact sheet: hearing protectors recommended at concerts; earmuffs 'come in sizes ... for adults and children' and are 'easier than earplugs to use correctly, especially for young children'. NIDCD Protect Your Child's Hearing: 'A parent should help especially young children insert earplugs, and make sure they are a good fit.' ASHA 2022: children better off with well-fitting earmuffs.

items.bewering: Hoe korter die harde klank aanhou, hoe minder skade doen dit aan jou ore.
items.blok: Hoe jy jou ore veilig hou
items.bron: WHO Make Listening Safe: 85 dB for eight hours or 100 dB for 15 minutes is unsafe, i.e. the safe time shrinks as level rises; NIDCD: harm from sounds that are 'both loud and long-lasting'. The lesson already notes the exception (one very loud bang does immediate damage).

items.bewering: Daar is baie redes waarom 'n mens sag hoor of nie kan hoor nie. Baie mense is so gebore, en harde geraas is nie altyd die rede nie.
items.blok: 'n Toestel wat klank harder maak
items.bron: WHO fact sheet 'Deafness and hearing loss' (who.int): causes include genetic factors (hereditary and non-hereditary) before birth, intrauterine infections such as rubella and CMV, childhood infections such as meningitis, ageing, and loud sound exposure.

items.bewering: 'n Gehoorapparaat is 'n klein toestel wat klank harder maak. Dit help baie mense wat sag hoor om te hoor wat rondom hulle gebeur.
items.blok: 'n Toestel wat klank harder maak
items.bron: NIDCD, Hearing Aids (nidcd.nih.gov/health/hearing-aids): 'a small electronic device that you wear in or behind your ear'; it 'makes some sounds louder so that a person with hearing loss can listen, communicate' and take part more fully in daily life.

items.bewering: Dit bring nie verlore gehoor terug nie, en dit help nie almal ewe veel nie.
items.blok: 'n Toestel wat klank harder maak
items.bron: NIDCD, Hearing Aids: 'A hearing aid will not restore your normal hearing'; benefit depends on surviving hair cells, there are 'practical limits to the amount of amplification', and where damage is too great 'a hearing aid would be ineffective'.

items.bewering: geraasbesoedeling: Klank wat hard, naar of skadelik is, of wat lank aanhou.
items.blok: begrip: geraasbesoedeling
items.bron: US EPA: noise is 'unwanted or disturbing sound'; SA law's noise nuisance is noise that 'disturbs or impairs ... the convenience or peace of any person' (BusinessTech 2019). Read alone, this entry drops the one element every definition rests on - that the sound is unwanted or bothers someone - which the study block supplies with 'Klank wat so pla'. As it stands, any sound that lasts long is noise pollution: a long song you enjoy, birdsong all morning, a quiet fridge hum nobody notices. A glossary entry is looked up on its own, so it must be true on its own.
items.regstelling: Put the bothering element into the entry and keep the four criteria under it, e.g. sound that bothers people because it is loud, unpleasant or harmful, or goes on too long ('Klank wat pla omdat dit hard, naar of skadelik is, of te lank aanhou'). This stays within the CAPS wording (hard, onaangenaam, skadelik, lang periode) and matches the study block's own frame.

items.bewering: permanent: Iets wat vir altyd so bly en nie weer regkom nie.
items.blok: begrip: permanent
items.bron: Wiktionary 'permanent' (adjective): 'without end; eternal'; 'lasting for an indefinitely long time'; Dutch 'permanent' glossed with 'blijvend', antonym 'tijdelijk'. The meaning is lasting/for ever; 'nie weer regkom nie' presupposes that something is broken, which is this lesson's context and not part of the word. Read alone, the entry teaches that only damage can be permanent, and it will mislead wherever the word describes something that is fine (a permanent home, a permanent marker, and the adult teeth that replace milk teeth). Minor, but the entry is not true on its own. (No Afrikaans dictionary page could be reached online; the cognate senses were used.)
items.regstelling: Define the word without the damage context, e.g. something that stays that way for ever ('Iets wat vir altyd so bly'). The study block already says the ear damage never comes right, so nothing is lost.

items.bewering: trommelvlies: 'n Dun velletjie in jou oor wat vibreer wanneer klank dit tref.
items.blok: begrip: trommelvlies
items.bron: NIDCD, How Do We Hear?: sound travels down the ear canal to the eardrum, and 'the eardrum vibrates from the incoming sound waves'. The eardrum is a thin membrane. True read alone.

items.bewering: gehoorapparaat: 'n Klein toestel wat klank harder maak vir iemand wat sag hoor.
items.blok: begrip: gehoorapparaat
items.bron: NIDCD, Hearing Aids: 'a small electronic device' that 'makes some sounds louder so that a person with hearing loss can listen'. True read alone.

opsomming: Every safety instruction checks out against NIDCD, CDC/NIOSH, ASHA, WHO and South African regulations (including hands over the ears, which NIDCD itself advises for a sudden loud noise), but four sentences need fixing: the damage sentence says a sound that only lasts long can harm hearing, when it must also be loud; 'too-loud sound breaks the hair cells' needs 'can', because ringing ears after a loud sound often recover; and read alone, the glossary entry for geraasbesoedeling drops the idea that the sound bothers someone, while the entry for permanent wrongly limits the word to something broken.
